title: Oncogene-induced tumor-like structures in Xenopus share hallmarks of human tumors

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Oncogene-induced tumor-like structures in Xenopus share hallmarks of human tumors

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Tumor-like structures induced in Xenopus laevis tadpoles by human oncogenes such as mutant KRAS display overproliferation, increased nuclear size, hypoxia, intracellular acidity and leukocyte attraction, hallmarks shared with classic human tumors.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In the Xenopus laevis tadpole model, we used human oncogenes such as mutant KRAS to drive formation of tumor-like structures that exhibited overproliferation, increased nuclear size, hypoxia, acidity, and leukocyte attraction.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Chernet BT, Levin M, “Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range”, Oncotarget (2014), doi:10.18632/oncotarget.1935; section “Abstract”. Scope: Induced tumor-like structures (ITLS) in Xenopus laevis embryos injected with Xrel3, Gli1 or KRASG12D mRNA

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2014-tumor-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Each listed hallmark has a standard assay and published measurements are available. Existing data can test the Xenopus phenotype but only partially address the comparison with the heterogeneous scope of human tumors.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify proliferation, nuclear area, hypoxia, intracellular pH, and leukocyte recruitment in oncogene-induced structures versus matched unaffected tissue, then compare effect directions with standard tumor hallmarks. Consistent significant differences support phenotypic similarity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Sharing hallmarks does not establish equivalence to human tumors.

Raw images and per-embryo measurements are not clearly deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.75
data existence: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.6

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Each named hallmark has a standard assay, so the resemblance claim is testable. The paper reports that the induced structures showed them, and the quantitative stain values are not deposited. Human tumor archives do not contain this Xenopus induction series, so the comparison cannot be redone from open data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In oncogene-induced tadpole structures, quantify proliferation, nuclear area, hypoxia, intracellular pH, and leukocyte markers against stage-matched tissue. A joint elevation matching the stated human-tumor hallmarks would support the resemblance; absence of several of those readouts would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The five hallmark measurements are not available as animal-level public data.

Tadpole induced structures can share some stains with human tumors while differing in others that were not scored.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.72
data adequacy: 0.3
analysis feasibility: 0.32
discriminating power: 0.38
